verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere documents official SDKs for Swift and Kotlin, a React Native (JavaScript) integration path, and claims "six thin bindings" over one C++ core. Its hosted endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so OpenAI's official Python and JS clients can call it via `base_url`, but those are third-party libraries, not RunAnywhere's own. missing for 10: a documented first-party Python SDK, a first-party JavaScript/Node or web client library beyond React Native, an explicit list of the six bindings' languages, and independent hands-on corroboration.
